scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC1, PC2, dc_pc5 (Campus 2 VLAN 5) report they cannot reach
their gateway 10.5.0.254 or anything beyond. Same Campus's
VLAN 6 PCs (PC3, PC4) are fine. switch4 link status looks UP,
sshswitch is healthy. Where's the break?

injection.action: shut down the VLAN 5 trunk subinterface (eth0.5)

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0.5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch4 eth0.5 (VLAN 5 trunk subinterface
  to sshswitch)
Mechanism: switch4 carries VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 to sshswitch
  via the eth0 trunk. The VLAN 5 sub-interface eth0.5 was
  brought down — VLAN 5 access PCs are now isolated from
  sshswitch's br_v5 SVI. VLAN 6 (eth0.6) is unaffected.
Localization: switch4 eth0.5
Root cause: VLAN 5 trunk subinterface down on switch4
Fix: `ip link set eth0.5 up` on switch4
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth0.5 up` on switch4

line.command: ip -br link show eth0.5 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a downed VLAN 5 trunk sub-interface on switch4. The switch
uses multiple Linux bridges to segment traffic by VLAN: br_vlan5 aggregates
the VLAN 5 access ports (eth1/eth2/eth3/eth6, all UP and forwarding), and
connects to the sshswitch uplink via the sub-interface eth0.5. That
sub-interface is administratively DOWN — confirmed by `ip link show eth0.5`
returning `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` (no UP flag) and bridge state "disabled".
The parallel sub-interface for VLAN 6, eth0.6, is fully UP and forwarding,
which is exactly why VLAN 6 PCs (PC3, PC4) reach their gateway 10.6.0.254
without issue. With eth0.5 down, VLAN 5 broadcast traffic (ARP for the
gateway at 10.5.0.254) cannot cross from switch4 into sshswitch, so PC1,
PC2, and dc_pc5 receive "Destination Host Unreachable" for every ping —
directly verified: PC1 → 10.5.0.254 is 100% loss. The sshswitch side is
healthy: br_v5 holds 10.5.0.254/24, bond0.5 and eth0.5 are both UP there,
and the gateway is reachable from the sshswitch LAN side. The root cause is
that switch4's eth0.5 VLAN 5 sub-interface was brought administratively
down, severing the only path from the VLAN 5 bridge to the rest of the
network. The fix is to bring it back up on switch4:
  ip link set eth0.5 up
This restores the trunk path and allows VLAN 5 ARP and data traffic to flow
through to sshswitch, immediately restoring gateway reachability for all
VLAN 5 hosts.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly names switch4 as the device with the downed eth0.5 VLAN 5 sub-interface.
The agent explicitly identifies the affected component as switch4's VLAN 5 trunk sub-interface eth0.5 and describes it as administratively down.
The report clearly separates VLAN 5 (eth0.5 down and isolated on switch4 affecting PC1/PC2/dc_pc5) from VLAN 6 (eth0.6 up and functioning), matching the required VLAN scope distinction.
Recommends running 'ip link set eth0.5 up' on switch4, which matches the expected fix to bring the VLAN 5 sub-interface back up.

The log contains direct observations (eth0.5 state DOWN on switch4, eth0.6 UP, VLAN5 hosts unable to reach 10.5.0.254 while VLAN6 works, and eth0.5 shown as master of br_vlan5) that support the agent's conclusion; the causal chain and checks are coherent and sufficient. One minor gap: explicit sshswitch output is truncated in the log, but the central evidence localizing the fault to switch4 eth0.5 is present.
